<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Frederica S. Wilson, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark Takano, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Summer L. Lee, Rep. Adelita S. Grijalva>: INTRODUCTION
H.R. 7894, the Truman Scholarship Clean House Act, sponsored by Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-NY), amends the Harry S Truman Memorial Scholarship Act to make significant changes to the operation of the Harry S. Truman Scholarship Foundation (``Truman Foundation'') and the processes by which recipients of the Harry S. Truman Memorial Scholarship (``Truman Scholars'') are selected. 19 million students enrolled in American higher education are facing a system that is becoming increasingly harder to access and afford. This is due in part to actions recently taken by this Committee.\1\ Given that context, the Majority has decided to focus the Committee's time and attention on a small program that provides graduate school scholarships to approximately 60 students yearly, to pursue careers in public service. The Majority does this under the rationale that the Truman Scholarship is riddled with political bias disfavoring conservative students and academic subjects of study.\2\
\1\Pub. Law. No. 119-21 Sec. Sec.  81001, 82001 (2025).
\2\Infra notes 3-32 and accompanying text.
H.R. 7894 is a bundle of policy ``solutions'' looking for a problem. The Committee has no credible evidence of wrongdoing or bias on behalf of the Foundation, relying instead on flimsy non-academic papers and ``exposes'' by entities with established conservative ties. It is not clear if the bill's policies would even bring about the Majority's desired solutions if passed into law. What is clear is that the bill would give President Trump power to remake the Scholarship as he saw fit. Based on the President's established track record of remaking political institutions with little regard to his authority or the law, this Committee should not empower him further.
BACKGROUND INTO TRUMAN SCHOLARSHIP ``OVERSIGHT''
Starting in the 118th Congress, the Majority has conducted oversight of the Truman Foundation based on allegations of left-wing bias. Because these allegations are the driving force behind all Committee action in regard to the Truman Foundation, it is important to analyze and dismiss them before addressing the substance of H.R. 7894.
On May 20th, 2024 then Committee Chair Virginia Foxx (R- NC), Higher Education and Workforce Development (HEWD) Subcommittee Chair Burgess Owens (R-UT), and Rep. Robert Aderholt (R-AL), Chair of the Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies of the Committee on Appropriations, sent a letter to Dr. Terry Babcock-Lumish, Executive Secretary of the Truman Foundation.\3\ The letter leveled accusations of bias at the Foundation, alleging it displayed a ``stark partisan tilt''.\4\ These accusations were based wholly on analysis conducted by scholars at the American Enterprise Institute, a right-wing think tank.\5\
\3\Letter from Rep. Virginia Foxx, H. Comm. on Educ. & the Workforce Chair., et al., to Dr. Terry Babcock-Lumish, Exec. Sec'y, The Harry S. Truman Scholarship Foundation (May 20, 2024), https:// edworkforce.house.gov/uploadedfiles/5.20.24_truman_letter.pdf.
\4\Id.
\5\Over the last two Congresses, Committee Republicans have called AEI scholars and fellows as witnesses at least eight different full Committee or subcommittee hearings.
In that AEI report, Frederick Hess and Joe Pitts alleged that the Rhodes Scholarship Program (privately funded) and Truman Scholarship Program (in part publicly funded) evinced left-wing bias in their recipient selection processes.\6\ In their report, Hess & Pitts conducted analysis of 182 Truman Scholar biographies from 2021-2023 and the Scholars' policy issue interests. The biographical analysis proved nothing; the majority of Truman Scholars could not be classified under AEI's standards as either progressive or conservative from a reading of their biographies.\7\ Further, their analysis found that 90 percent of Scholars reported no affiliation with partisan officials, candidates, or organizations in their biographies.\8\
\6\Letter from Rep. Virginia Foxx, supra note 3; Frederick M. Hess & Joe Pitts, Do the Rhodes and Truman Scholarships Have Any Room for the Right? Am. Enterprise Inst., May 2024, https://www.aei.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Do-the-Rhodes-and-Truman-Scholarships-Have-Any- Room-for-the-Right.pdf?x85095.
\7\Hess & Pitts, supra note 6, at 3 (``After examining the biographies, we concluded that there weren't enough data on affiliation with partisan officials, candidates, or organizations to support credible analysis. While scholars were vastly more likely to report left-leaning associations than right-leaning ones, more than 90 percent didn't report any such affiliation.'').
\8\Id.
Researchers with no pre-conceived notions regarding the Truman Foundation might have stopped there. However, Hess & Pitts continued to a strained policy issue analysis classifying policy issues that Truman Scholars expressed interest in as ``progressive,'' ``centrist,'' or ``conservative.''\9\ Progressive issues included: LGBT+ advocacy; racial justice and diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI); climate and the environment; and immigration rights. Centrist issues included mental health, cybersecurity and technology, national and international security and sexual violence prevention. Conservative issues included free markets, religious freedom, pro-life advocacy, and gun rights.
\9\Id. at 3-5. Hess & Pitts coded the scholars' policy issue interests by 12 categories, four belonging to each ideological framework. They emphasized that each policy issue category was ``uncontested'' and therefore is unarguably belonging to its respective ideological framework.
Hess & Pitts found ``[O]f the 182 Truman scholars, 74 cite interest in at least one progressive issue, while just six note interest in a conservative issue.''\10\ This was seen by them as a damning indictment of the Truman Scholarship as being overrun with progressive scholars. That analysis fails to mention by their own standards, if a survey of 182 scholars showed that 80 scholars expressed interest in partisan policy issues, that leaves 102 of scholars who expressed interest in policy issues that could not be classified as either progressive or conservative. To put this in terms our Majority colleagues might better understand, the percentage of scholars who expressed either centrist or non-partisan policy issue interests (56%) is greater than the current percentage of House Republicans' majority in Congress (50.58%).\11\
\10\Id.at 4.
\11\Based on the Clerk of the House's tally of 218 Republicans, 212 Democrats, 1 Independent, and 4 vacancies. If the Independent who caucuses with the Republicans is included, their majority is 50.81%.
A sober conclusion could be drawn that Truman Scholars on the whole were mostly interested in centrist or non-partisan policy issues. Hess & Pitts instead called on the Truman Foundation to recruit a more diverse scholar pool that ``true to the nation's breadth of perspectives, views, and values'' and on institutions to reevaluate their engagement with the Foundation if matters do not improve.\12\ This request was then parroted in the May 20th letter from Reps. Foxx, Owens and Aderholt.\13\
\12\Hess & Pitts, supra note 6, at 5.
\13\Letter from Rep. Virginia Foxx, supra note 3, at 1-2 (``. . . the Truman Scholarship should, at a bare minimum, be reflective of the country's breadth of values, viewpoints, and interests.'') (no internal citations omitted).
In response to the May 20th letter highlighting the AEI study,\14\ Executive Secretary of the Foundation, Dr. Terry Babcock-Lumish responded with a comprehensive critique of the AEI analysis for its broad characterization of issues as conservative or progressive.\15\ She also called the findings misleading because the researchers did not acknowledge all applicants, only those students who were selected.\16\ Dr. Babcock-Lumish claimed that the Foundation has no knowledge of applicants' ideological orientations unless they explicitly share them.\17\ She criticized the researcher's methods flagging that categorizing an issue as conservative, progressive, or neutral is subjective.\18\ She added that in the report ``[e]ven within issues, there is no allowance made for students who wish to take a conservative approach to a topic already deemed `progressive.'''\19\ Dr. Babcock-Lumish also noted that AEI ignored the fact that applicants work in apolitical settings where they are required to avoid partisan politics. Therefore, most applicants are neither obviously progressive nor obviously conservative. For example, she noted that ``a Naval Academy midshipman interested in studying the environmental impacts of the nuclear fleet would be characterized as progressive for the purposes of AEI's report.''\20\ Similarly, at a December 3, 2025 HEWD Subcommittee Hearing on the Truman Foundation, Ranking Member Bobby Scott (D-VA) challenged the report's classification of certain policy issues as inherently progressive:

Mr. Scott. Well, you consider left leaning if you
have an interest in racial justice?
Mr. Hess. Yes, right. DEI in particular was coded
as----
Mr. Scott. Racial justice? That's not a universal
kind of idea, but that's a left leaning, disqualifying
fact. Do you need to balance that off with people that
oppose racial justice?
Mr. Hess. No, sir.
. . .
Mr. Scott. Okay. Climate change is a left leaning
idea, is that right?
Mr. Hess. That's how we coded it sir, that's right.
Mr. Scott. Okay. Now, how many college students fail
to recognize the scientific fact of climate change?
Mr. Hess. I don't----
Mr. Scott. What portion of college students fail to
recognize the scientific fact of climate change?
Mr. Hess. I don't know.
Mr. Scott. What portion of college faculty--
prospective, college faculty can get hired if they say
they don't believe in science?
Mr. Hess. [no response.]
Mr. Scott. Not many.\21\
\21\Public Funds, Private Politics: Examining Bias in the Truman Scholarship Program: Hearing Before the Subcomm. on Higher Educ. & Workforce Development of the H. Comm. on Educ. & Workforce, 119th Cong.
(2025) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ddGJVRQSOeY&t=5224s.
Committee Oversight of the Truman Foundation was also driven by ``reporting'' from The College Fix, a conservative leaning news website. In June 2024, The College Fix published an ``expose'' on the Truman Scholarship and political ideology.\22\ Using a combination of winners' official biographies, self-reported work histories on LinkedIn, and social media profiles and posts, the author's found that of the 599 recipients since 2015, only 26 leaned right, 354 leaned left.\23\ Politics could not be determined for 219 of the 599 recipients.\24\ Moreover, of 380 scholars with political affiliations, 93% were ``affiliated'' with left leaning politics.\25\
\22\The College Fix, The College Fix investigates: Truman Scholarships, (June 10, 2024), https://www.thecollegefix.com/bulletin-board/the-college-fix-investigates-truman-scholarships/.
